sequence_description: Test whether Casdoor enforces assertion-level signature integrity when the application is configured to require signed assertions. Hypothesis: SP may accept an attacker-signed SAMLResponse even when Enable SAML assertion signature is enabled, indicating verification policy is not applied to the consumed semantic proof (response vs assertion signature confusion).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_saml_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_saml_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Expected secure behavior: attacker-signed forged SAMLResponse must be rejected, especially when assertion signatures are required by application policy.

sequence_description: Replay a SAML assertion that includes <OneTimeUse/> using the same Assertion/@ID twice. First login is a control (should succeed). Second login should be rejected if OneTimeUse and/or replay cache is enforced.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_onetimeuse_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_onetimeuse_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replayed OneTimeUse assertion (second submission should be rejected)

sequence_description: Test whether Casdoor rejects replay of the same SAML Assertion/@ID after the first session is explicitly logged out (replay cache must survive logout).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_victim_saml2_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_victim_saml2_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replay of the same SAML Assertion/@ID after logout (replay cache not enforced across logout)

sequence_description: Test whether replay detection is incorrectly scoped to principal/session by replaying the same Assertion/@ID for a different upstream principal (should still be rejected).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_bob_saml2_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_bob_saml2_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replay of the same SAML Assertion/@ID for a different principal (replay detection incorrectly scoped)

sequence_description: Test whether an application config change (exclusive sign-in enabled) causes SAML NotOnOrAfter enforcement to regress, allowing expired assertions to be accepted on subsequent logins.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_victim_cfg_saml2_expired_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_victim_cfg_saml2_expired_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted an expired SAML assertion after application config change (NotOnOrAfter not enforced)

sequence_description: Replay a OneTimeUse SAML assertion ID across two different upstream principals (victim then attacker) to test whether OneTimeUse/replay cache is incorrectly scoped to principal/session and allows reuse.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_replay_onetimeuse_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_replay_onetimeuse_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replayed OneTimeUse assertion ID for a different principal; OneTimeUse/replay cache may be incorrectly scoped.

sequence_description: Control valid SAML login, then rotate SAML provider metadata (simulating IdP key rollover) and attempt an expired assertion. Tests whether time validity checks regress or are bypassed after provider metadata update.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_expired_post_rotation_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_expired_post_rotation_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted an expired SAML assertion after provider metadata rotation; NotOnOrAfter enforcement may be bypassed/regressed.

sequence_description: Control SAML login, then change application CookieExpireInHours (sentinel/TTL-related config) and attempt replay of the same Assertion/@ID. Tests whether replay cache is incorrectly tied to cookie/session TTL config and becomes ineffective after change.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_replay_after_change_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_replay_after_change_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replay of the same SAML Assertion/@ID after application TTL/cookie config change; replay cache may be reset or improperly scoped.

sequence_description: Attempt to skip the required SP-initiated SAML flow by directly POSTing a forged SAMLResponse to Casdoor login endpoint without first initiating an auth flow (no state/RelayState context). Flow coherence requires rejection.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_direct_saml_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_direct_saml_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Flow coherence violated: Casdoor accepted a SAMLResponse without an SP-initiated flow context (step skipping / missing state/RelayState binding).

sequence_description: Create a second SAML provider and attempt to initiate an auth flow expecting provider-saml-test, then submit a SAMLResponse via saml_login referencing a different provider (provider-saml-alt-i3). Flow coherence requires binding to the selected provider.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_provider_switch_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_provider_switch_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Flow coherence violated: Casdoor accepted a SAMLResponse under a different provider than the one implied/selected by the initiated flow (cross-provider splicing).

sequence_description: Attack: Control SAML login with valid assertion, then attempt SAML login with expired assertion. If accepted, try token_exchange requesting a different audience via resource indicator-like behavior (modeled as exchanging at a second client). Expectation: expired assertion rejected; if not, exchange should still not allow cross-client audience confusion.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_expired_saml_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_expired_saml_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted expired SAML assertion, violating time-bound upstream intent (I5).

sequence_description: I5 attack: tighten broker policy by changing application tags to exclude a user, verify password login is blocked, then attempt SAML login for same user to see if external SAML bypasses tag-based authorization policy.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_saml_tag_bypass_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_saml_tag_bypass_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SAML login bypassed application tag restriction that blocks password login; broker policy not bound across auth methods (I5).

sequence_description: Test whether replaying a OneTimeUse SAML assertion yields a second valid session (authorization binding broken because a one-time upstream intent is accepted multiple times). Includes control login then replay with identical Assertion/@ID.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_saml_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_saml_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted a replayed OneTimeUse SAML assertion, granting a second session beyond upstream one-time intent

sequence_description: Create a second SAML provider with different metadata/issuer, then attempt to authenticate through provider-A while forging Issuer to provider-B (issuer confusion). Expect rejection; acceptance could grant permissions under the wrong broker policy/provider trust context.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_issuer_mismatch_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_issuer_mismatch_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted an assertion whose Issuer corresponds to a different provider, risking cross-provider authorization/policy confusion
